Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

In this session, we will solve problems on homogeneous functions and Euler's theorem.

Key details

  • Remember, here n can be positive, negative.
  • Or even zero.
  • Then we are left out with x power 4 plus 2x square y square plus y power 4.
  • In the denominator we get lambda power 4 of x square plus y square whole square.
  • After lambda power 4, lambda power 4, we can write 1 to be lambda power 0.
  • U equals sine inverse of y by x divided by square root of x square plus y square.
  • Replace x by lambda x, replace y by lambda y.
  • Sign in us of lambda y by lambda x.
  • And in the denominate denominator, it is square root of lambda x whole square plus lambda y whole square.
  • U equals x square y plus xy square divided by x plus y power 3.
  • U equals e power x minus e power minus y divided by x minus y.
  • This simplification doesn't give us lambda power n times u of x comma y.
  • It means u of lambda x comma lambda y is not equal to lambda power n times u of x comma y.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let us solve the first problem u equals x power four plus two times x square into y square plus y power four divided by x square plus y square one square.
  • Now in order to test whether the given function is homogeneous or not, we need to prove this particular condition that is u of lambda x comma lambda y equals lambda power n times u of x comma y.
  • In the given function, we replace x by lambda x, y by lambda y.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

I hope the concept of homogeneous function is clear to you.

Key details

  • If u equal to x minus y divided by x square plus y square, then find the value of x into dou u by dou x.
  • plus y into dou u by dou y and x square into dou square u by dou x square plus 2 x y into dou square u by dou x into dou y plus y square into dou square u by dou y square.
  • As we know that this is nothing but extension of Euler's theorem.
  • So in order to use Euler's theorem, first we need to prove that u is a homogeneous function of degree n.
  • We get to know that u is a homogeneous function of degree minus 1 because u of lambda x comma lambda y equals lambda power minus 1 times u of x comma y.
  • After proving u to be homogeneous function, we can directly use Euler's formula, which is nothing but x into dou by dou x plus y into dou by dou y equals n u.
  • Because n is minus 1, we can get this particular answer that is x into dou by dou x plus y into dou by dou y equals minus u becomes minus half x minus y divided by x square plus y square.
  • Because n is minus 1, finally we get 2 times.
  • X minus y divided by x square plus y square.
  • U of x comma y becomes log u, then this part becomes x power 3 times y power 3 divided by x square plus y square.
  • Then check whether f of u is homogeneous or not.
  • After we simplify, we get lambda power x power 3 y power 3 divided by lambda square of x square plus y square.
  • equals n times f of u by f dash of u.
  • If u equal to log of x square plus y square divided by x plus y, then find a value of these two.
  • Again observe carefully.
  • Again, we use a different approach because log is involved, we take exponential on both the sides.

Example or application from the lecture

  • After understanding the concept of homogeneous functions, let us solve problems on Euler's theorem.
  • It is given that u equals e power x power 3 times y power 3 divided by x square plus y square, then find the value of x into dou u by dou x plus y into dou u by dou y using euler's theorem.
  • Observe carefully, the given function is not homogeneous.
